newsitem.title: FRANCE: Foreign crises should be part of French vote - Leotard.
newsitem.headline: Foreign crises should be part of French vote - Leotard.

text.p: France's ruling centre-right coalition wants international crises like Algeria, the Middle East and Zaire discussed in the country's current parliamentary election campaign, one of its leaders said on Tuesday.

"There can be no silence about Algeria which is today at the mercy of a form of barbarism," said Francois Leotard, president of the Union for French Democracy (UDF), junior coalition partner of the Rally for the Republic Gaullists.

"We will propose during this campaign that the future parliamentary majority back the democrats in Algeria who are engaged in a very difficult struggle," Leotard told reporters at a briefing he addressed with Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

The centre-right cabinets which governed France since 1993, including when Leotard was defence minister from 1993-1995, steered clear of open involvement in the Algerian crisis which several times spilled over into France, including bouts of terror bombings and a hijack of a French airliner.

On the Middle East, Leotard said "the peace process must absolutely resume and it must allow the Palestinians to regain the confidence they have lost in the good faith of their negotiating partners (the Israelis)."
Leotard said that in Zaire and the region, "France must remain the constant defender of human rights, of democracy, of the refusal of one-party states and in favour of minorities."
Paris has been strongly criticised abroad for its support of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.
